planting.note: Direct sow in early spring or fall; Coastal Star is a heat-tolerant romaine bred to hold full-size, heavy hearts and resist bolting longer than standard romaine types, extending the spring harvest window before summer heat sets in.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Coastal Star is a dark green romaine bred for heat tolerance and slow bolting, producing full-size, dense, heavy hearts even as temperatures climb toward the point where most romaine varieties turn bitter and send up a seed stalk. The upright heads have crisp, sweet leaves with excellent texture through to the crunchy heart. Provide afternoon shade during the hottest stretches of a Gulf Coast spring to further extend the harvest window, and keep soil consistently moist, since drought stress accelerates bolting even in heat-tolerant varieties. Harvest whole heads once hearts have filled out, or pick outer leaves as a cut-and-come-again crop.

common_name: Two Star Lettuce (Slow-Bolt Dark Green Leaf Lettuce)

planting.note: Direct sow in early spring or fall; Two Star is a dark green Waldmann's-type leaf lettuce bred to bolt roughly a week later than standard Waldmann's Green while holding good flavor into warm weather, useful for stretching the Gulf Coast spring lettuce season.

directions: Sow directly 1/4 inch deep in fertile, well-drained soil; Two Star is a dark green, savoyed leaf lettuce bred as a slower-bolting improvement on the classic Waldmann's Green type, holding its mild, sweet flavor and tender texture longer into warm weather before turning bitter and running to seed. The loose, upright rosette of ruffled leaves is well suited to cut-and-come-again harvesting, letting a single planting supply salads over several weeks. Provide afternoon shade during hot spells to further slow bolting, and keep soil evenly moist, since drought stress speeds up flowering in any leaf lettuce. Sow successively every 2-3 weeks through the cool season for a steady, continuous harvest.
sources: seed catalog reference (Harris Seeds, Territorial Seed Company, Stokes Seeds)

planting.note: Start indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost for spring, or midsummer for fall; Diplomat carries resistance to downy mildew and shows good tolerance of both heat and cold, giving it flexibility across the Gulf South's fall, winter, and spring broccoli windows.

directions: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before setting out transplants into rich, evenly moist soil; Diplomat is a broccoli hybrid bred with resistance to downy mildew, a fungal disease that thrives in the cool, damp weather typical of a Gulf South winter broccoli crop and can otherwise blemish and stunt developing heads. It forms dense, uniform, blue-green heads on a plant that tolerates both heat during establishment and cold during head development, giving it flexibility across spring and fall plantings. After the central head is cut, side shoots continue to develop, extending the harvest for several more weeks. Cut the main head while the buds are still tight and before any yellow petals show, then keep harvesting side shoots as they reach a similar tight-bud stage.
sources: seed catalog reference (Stokes Seeds, Harris Seeds, Holmes Seed Company)

planting.note: Start indoors and transplant in late summer for a fall-through-winter crop; Marathon is a Sakata-bred industry-standard hybrid noted for exceptional cold tolerance and reliable overwintering, including documented success as a winter crop in Florida — a strong fit for the Gulf Coast's mild winter growing window.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil in late summer for a fall and winter crop, or in late winter for an early spring crop; Marathon is a broccoli hybrid recognized industry-wide for exceptional cold tolerance, holding up through hard frosts and cold snaps that would damage less hardy varieties while continuing to develop a large, dense, tightly beaded blue-green head. This cold hardiness makes it especially well suited to the Gulf South's mild winter growing window, where it can be grown as a true overwintering crop instead of racing to beat summer heat. After the main head is harvested, the plant produces a strong flush of side shoots for continued picking. Cut heads while the buds are still tight, before any yellow flower color shows.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Broccoli Production

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting for an early spring crop; Farao is one of the earliest-maturing fresh-market cabbage hybrids available, bred for resistance to tip burn and to hold in the field without splitting, letting Gulf Coast gardeners bring in a cabbage crop before summer heat arrives.

directions: Start seeds indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; harden off before transplanting to full sun in fertile, well-drained soil; Farao is one of the earliest-maturing fresh-market cabbage hybrids available, forming compact, round, 2-3 lb heads that size up quickly, an advantage for Gulf Coast gardeners racing to finish a spring cabbage crop before summer heat sets in. It is bred for resistance to tip burn, a physiological disorder that browns and damages inner leaves under fluctuating moisture and heat, and holds well in the field for a week or more past maturity without splitting. The mild, tender heads work well fresh in slaw or lightly cooked. Because of its early maturity, Farao is also a good choice for a second, fall planting timed to mature before the first hard freeze.
